set.body:
Objective:
Provide one elegant, typed workflow from an fMRIPrep-like BIDS project through first-level fMRI regression and group analysis to durable first- and second-level results, without loading the study or full spatial domain into memory.

Architecture:
- Add fmri-workflow as the outer composition module. It owns study specifications, catalog compilation, cross-level dependencies, provenance, resume policy, and lowering to pipeline plans; lower modules must not depend back on it.
- Keep reusable contracts in their natural modules: BIDS discovery and entities in bids; run/time/sample geometry and lazy response sources in dataset; scientific model plans in model; prepared work and kernels in fit; second-level kernels in group; generic DAGs and receipts in pipeline; format-specific IO in JVM adapters.
- Plans and work units are immutable serializable data. Artifact tables carry catalog, manifest, and storage references rather than matrices or captured closures.
- Parallelism is expressed as scheduler-neutral work over independent first-level units and spatial blocks. Time is not split within a run. Implement local sequential and bounded-parallel interpreters first; do not couple core code to Spark, Slurm, or a JVM-only scheduler.
- Output is a typed sink capability with transactional finalization. BIDS-like bundled and individual named NIfTI maps are supported through manifests, while additional stores remain pluggable adapters.

Non-negotiable constraints:
- Bounded memory by configured spatial block size except where an engine explicitly declares a global-reduction preparation topology.
- Exact subject, session, task, run, TR, space, mask, sample-order, and provenance identity at every boundary.
- Deterministic work IDs, idempotent writes, retryable units, durable receipts, and resumable first-to-second-level handoff.
- Compressed NIfTI input uses an explicit staging or cache policy rather than pretending gzip is random-access.
- No naive full-study GroupData or response materialization in the required execution path.

Epic acceptance:
1. A realistic multi-subject, multi-session or multi-run fMRIPrep-style fixture compiles from BIDS discovery into typed first-level units using header-first validation.
2. The fixture runs first-level design, regression, and contrasts blockwise, writes a durable first-level catalog and named-map manifests, then runs group analysis from that catalog and writes second-level outputs.
3. Sequential and bounded-parallel execution produce equivalent scientific results within explicit tolerances, with deterministic ordering and stable work identities.
4. An interrupted run resumes without recomputing completed units or exposing partial finalized outputs.
5. Verification demonstrates that peak payload memory scales with configured block size rather than study size for the supported path.
6. Shared contracts and tests pass on JVM and Scala.js; JVM-only IO and staging adapters are tested separately.
7. Documentation includes the module ownership map, execution semantics, supported output layouts, and one end-to-end example.

Out of initial scope:
Concrete Spark or cluster adapters, remote object-store implementations, and complete HDF5 or GDS writers. The contracts must admit them without requiring them for epic completion.
set.title: Epic: out-of-core BIDS-to-group fMRI workflow
